401: A is correct because deploying the application on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones removes any single point of failure in the application tier and allows capacity to scale automatically with user demand. An Amazon RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ configuration keeps a synchronous standby copy in a separate Availability Zone and fails over automatically, which directly prevents the kind of data loss the company suffered when its self-managed database server crashed. The other options either concentrate resources in a single Availability Zone, depend on asynchronous replication that cannot guarantee data durability, or attempt an unsupported database pattern using EBS Multi-Attach.
402: A is correct because a Kinesis data stream with default settings retains records for only 24 hours, and since the application consumes the data only every other day, records are expiring from the stream before they can be read and written to Amazon S3. Extending the data retention period so it exceeds 48 hours ensures every record sent to Kinesis Data Streams remains available until the consumer processes it. This is a retention problem rather than a throughput, producer, or S3 problem, so adding shards, switching to the KPL, or enabling S3 Versioning would not resolve the data loss.
403: D is correct because a Lambda function obtains its permissions through the IAM execution role it assumes at runtime, so creating a role with the required Amazon S3 permissions and attaching it to the function is the correct way to grant the upload capability. IAM users with long-lived credentials are intended for human or external principals and are not how Lambda gains access to other services, and a resource policy on the function governs who may invoke the function rather than what the function itself can access.
404: D is correct because the marketing campaign produced a burst of S3 event notifications that outpaced the Lambda function, and S3 event notifications do not retry on failure, so documents were dropped without processing. Inserting an Amazon SQS queue between the bucket and the function buffers the surge, decouples the producers from the processing, and lets Lambda pull and retry each message until it is handled successfully. This makes the architecture reliable under spiky workloads without losing documents.
405: D and E are correct. D is correct because a target tracking scaling policy automatically adds and removes EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group to hold CPU utilization at a target level, which handles the significant traffic increases during working hours. E is correct because scheduled scaling can set the group's minimum, maximum, and desired capacity to zero for weekends and restore the default values at the start of the week, matching capacity to the known weekly demand pattern and eliminating cost while the system is not required. The ALB and the internet gateway are managed services that scale on their own, and deploying in multiple Regions adds cost without being required.
406: C and D are correct. C is correct because a security group on the web servers that allows inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 443 gives internet clients HTTPS access to the public subnet tier. D is correct because a security group on the DB instance that allows inbound traffic on port 3306 from the web servers' security group restricts database access to exactly the web tier, and referencing a security group instead of a subnet CIDR block keeps the rule tightly scoped to the web servers themselves. Security groups are stateful and cannot contain deny rules, and a subnet CIDR-based rule would be broader than the least privilege requirement.
407: D is correct because Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed, native Lustre file system that the application's existing Lustre clients can access directly while delivering the high throughput and low latency that gaming and HPC-style workloads require. AWS DataSync is a data transfer service rather than a mountable shared file system, a Storage Gateway file gateway exposes SMB or NFS shares rather than Lustre, and Amazon EFS uses the NFS protocol and cannot be configured to support Lustre clients.
408: B is correct because the remote devices communicate over UDP, which only a Network Load Balancer can handle, whereas an Application Load Balancer supports only HTTP and HTTPS traffic. AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes user traffic over the AWS global network to the closest healthy Regional endpoint, which minimizes latency for geographically dispersed devices and provides near-instant client failover to the other Region when an endpoint becomes unhealthy. A Route 53 failover routing policy relies on DNS, which can be slow to propagate because of resolver caching, making it inferior for rapid cross-Region failover.
409: C is correct because Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed native Windows file system that provides standard SMB shares, so the IIS web servers can continue using the same file share protocols and credentials with no application changes. It also offers Multi-AZ deployment options and automatic backups, making it the most resilient and durable replacement for the on-premises NAS. Amazon EFS uses NFS and targets Linux workloads, Amazon RDS is a database service, and AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid caching tier rather than a durable cloud-native file share.
410: B is correct because creating the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes ensures all data at rest on those volumes, as well as their snapshots, is encrypted with AWS KMS keys, with the EBS service handling the encryption transparently. IAM roles and instance tags have no effect on the encryption state of storage, and a KMS key policy controls who can use a key rather than whether new volumes are created encrypted.
411: C is correct because Aurora Serverless is MySQL-compatible, so the existing MySQL database can be migrated without any code or schema modifications. Because usage is sporadic with heavy bursts at the start of the month and unpredictable patterns during the week, Aurora Serverless automatically and rapidly scales database capacity up and down and pauses when idle, so the company pays only for the database capacity it actually consumes. A continuously provisioned RDS instance or self-managed MySQL on EC2 would incur cost during all the idle periods, and DynamoDB would require application changes.
412: D is correct because the S3 Block Public Access feature applied at the account level blocks public access to every bucket and object across the entire AWS account, which directly satisfies the requirement that all objects remain private. The service control policy created in AWS Organizations then prevents IAM users from disabling that setting, locking the protection in place and making the solution preventive rather than reactive. Approaches based on GuardDuty, Trusted Advisor, or Resource Access Manager only detect or notify after a change occurs and require additional remediation logic, rather than preventing public exposure outright.
413: B is correct because Amazon SES is a fully managed email service that handles the delivery infrastructure, scaling, bounce handling, and deliverability of marketing and transactional email, which eliminates the complex email delivery issues the company is resolving and removes the operational overhead of managing them. Sending email directly from web instances or from dedicated self-managed EC2 tiers leaves the company owning those same delivery problems. Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service rather than a high-volume application email delivery platform.
414: B is correct because an Amazon S3 File Gateway presents a standard SMB network share that maps directly to an S3 bucket, so the business system can keep saving its CSV reports to a network share exactly as it does today, and the files land in S3 in near real time with no scripting or scheduled jobs. The gateway manages transfer and upload automatically, which delivers the least administrative overhead of the options. DataSync with a scheduled task is only a daily batch, a custom DataSync API application requires development and maintenance, and an SFTP endpoint with an upload script adds ongoing script overhead.
415: A is correct because S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on their actual access patterns, with monitoring and tiering performed automatically at no retrieval or monitoring charge, which optimizes cost for every bucket without any analysis or manual intervention. Because the company does not know the access patterns of its data, a lifecycle rule transitioning objects to Intelligent-Tiering removes the need to predict usage per bucket. Storage class analysis requires evaluation and manual movement of objects, and blanket transitions to Glacier Instant Retrieval or One Zone-IA assume infrequent access that may not fit, while One Zone-IA also reduces resilience by storing data in a single Availability Zone.
416: B and D are correct. B is correct because an Amazon CloudFront distribution caches both static and dynamic content at edge locations close to the company's global users, which reduces latency and dramatically improves page load times for a worldwide audience. D is correct because a read replica for the RDS DB instance offloads read queries from the primary instance, so the OLTP database no longer contends between serving the application's reads and its writes, which improves overall performance as traffic increases. Amazon Redshift is an analytics warehouse rather than an OLTP performance fix, dynamic content cannot simply be hosted in S3, and Multi-AZ improves availability rather than read throughput.
417: C is correct because a Compute Savings Plan provides flexible discounts that automatically apply to both EC2 instance usage and Lambda usage in exchange for a one-year commitment, which maximizes savings across all the application's compute resources even as the number of Lambda functions grows. Connecting the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances gives them direct network access to those instances, keeping network latency between the services low. An EC2 Instance Savings Plan covers only EC2 and would not capture the Lambda savings, and leaving the functions in the Lambda service VPC would not provide the required direct private network access.
418: B is correct because adding the development account as a principal in the trust policy of the IAM role in the production account lets the existing development account users assume that role to access the production S3 bucket through standard cross-account role assumption. This complies with least privilege because team members keep only their current development permissions and gain production access solely through the tightly scoped role policy, with no new or broad credentials. Attaching Administrator Access is excessive, turning off S3 Block Public Access would expose data, and creating separate users in the production account duplicates identity management and credential sprawl.
419: C and E are correct. C is correct because an SCP attached to the root organizational unit that denies the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false prevents any IAM user or even the root user in every account from creating unencrypted EBS volumes, enforcing the security policy centrally while leaving normal encrypted volume creation unaffected. E is correct because specifying the Default EBS volume encryption setting enables EBS encryption by default, so every new EBS volume created for EC2 instances in the Region is encrypted automatically and employees can continue creating volumes exactly as they do today with no change to their workflow. Together these steps enforce and enable encryption at rest for all new volumes with minimal effect on employees.
420: D is correct because an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment keeps two readable standby DB instances in different Availability Zones and provides automatic failover that typically completes in under 35 seconds, meeting the requirement for failover in less than 40 seconds. The cluster exposes a reader endpoint that automatically routes read traffic to a readable standby, offloading reads from the primary instance without the cost and overhead of separate read replicas, which keeps costs low. A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment fails over more slowly, its standby is not readable, and adding standalone read replicas increases both cost and administrative complexity.
